findings.detail: Graph counts are accumulated by treating every train row's history-plus-target as a complete sequence. In the frozen next-item training format these rows are prefix/target observations, so earlier transitions are counted repeatedly (and the multiplicity varies with prefix length). This does not implement one increment per adjacent pair in each training sequence; it changes both C and the degree correction, and therefore the graph being applied.
findings.reproduction: For one user sequence [a,b,c], if train rows are ([a],b) and ([a,b],c), this code yields C[a,b]=2 and C[b,c]=1, whereas counting the observed sequence once yields C[a,b]=1 and C[b,c]=1. A sequence with more prefix rows inflates its early edges further.
findings.correction: Construct counts from the frozen training sequence representation exactly once per original training sequence, or deduplicate/reconstruct sequence events from the training rows before counting. Keep validation/test out of that construction.
